subject: Chemistry
title: Humphry Davy's Electric Elements
description: A quick win: understand Humphry Davy's Electric Elements.

hook.text: Humphry Davy used a giant battery to rip apart compounds nobody had ever broken before—and found new elements.

buildup.text: In 1807, he passed electric current through molten potash. A shiny metal appeared on the electrode.

discovery.text: He had isolated potassium. Within weeks, he did the same with sodium—two elements never seen before.

twist.text: Davy discovered potassium, sodium, calcium, barium, magnesium, and boron—all with electricity.

climax.text: He proved electricity could unlock nature's building blocks. Electrochemistry was born.

punchline.text: One battery, six new elements. Davy rewrote the table.

quiz.question: How did Humphry Davy discover new elements?
options: By passing electricity through molten compounds
By heating rocks to extreme temperatures

details.summary: Humphry Davy used Volta's newly invented battery to isolate six elements in just two years (1807-1808): sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, barium, and strontium. Electrolysis split stable compounds that no chemical method could decompose, revolutionizing element discovery overnight.
details.whyItMatters: Davy proved that electricity could unlock elements hidden in stable compounds, opening an entirely new method of element discovery. His work demonstrated that many common substances were actually compounds of unknown metals.
takeaways: Davy isolated six new elements using electrolysis in just two years
Potassium was so reactive it burst into flame when exposed to water
Electrolysis became a fundamental method for element discovery and production

faq.question: Why couldn't sodium and potassium be discovered before the electric battery?
faq.answer: Sodium and potassium bind to other elements so strongly that no chemical reagent or temperature available to early chemists could separate them. The battery provided the electrical energy needed to overcome these powerful chemical bonds..

faq.question: How did Davy react when he first isolated potassium?
faq.answer: According to his cousin and assistant Edmund Davy, Humphry danced around the laboratory in ecstatic delight when small metallic globules appeared at the electrode and burst into flame on contact with water. It was one of the most dramatic moments in the history of element discovery.
